## Finding 1 — FIXED: execute() cannot run from a worktree

Old find_root() walked up from the script's dir requiring isdir(.git); in a git worktree .git is a FILE carrying a gitdir: pointer, so root detection failed and execute() refused to run. New find_root() prefers `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (accepts both a .git dir and a .git file), treats absence of git as a loud die() (exit 2, stderr names the directory and git's own error — never a guess), and adds a sanity guard: the resolved root must contain this harness at <root>/tools/bakeoff.sh (realpath-compared), else it refuses to guess. The guard is the answer to 'a root detector that silently picks the wrong directory is how a lane would read the keys' — e.g. a copy of the harness inside an unrelated nested repo now dies instead of running lanes against the wrong checkout.

## Finding 2 — HONESTED + CHEAP HARDENING: the boundary is relative-path-only

Documentation first (docs/infra/bakeoff.md, new subsection 'Worktree execution and the isolation boundary'): the worktree isolation is stated as a RELATIVE-PATH boundary plus a convention (harness header instructs no shell commands; race briefs self-contained), NOT a sandbox. 'Do not describe worktree isolation as a guarantee.' A tool-using lane can read the main checkout's gitignored untracked/ via absolute paths; verified from inside lane-wt-t376: untracked/race-keys/ and untracked/race-grading/ absent from the lane's view (relative), and `test -f /Users/alex/Project/Zig/weizigo/untracked/race-keys/race1.key` returns true (absolute reach exists — demonstrated with existence only, no content read). NOTE: untracked/msg/milestone-01-ko-reframe/STATE.md IS tracked in git, so a worktree does contain that one file; the key/grading state is gitignored and absent.

Cheap hardening: execute() now records isolation.root / isolation.root_is_worktree / isolation.lane_cwd (+ a strength string) in lanes.json and prints `root=<root> worktree=<bool>` on stdout, so every run document can state exactly what a lane could reach. Lanes already dispatch with cwd=root (the worktree root when run from a worktree), so relative traversal cannot climb back to the main checkout.

NOT built this row (sized finding, per brief 'do not build a sandbox'): true isolation needs OS-level sandboxing (macOS seatbelt / Linux bwrap) or per-family tool restriction. pi has `--no-tools` (verified in `pi --help`), so deepseek/ollama lanes COULD be tool-restricted with one argv flag, but claude lanes legitimately need tools per brief (mechanical anchors: 'zig build test passes' is a scored criterion, §3.5) and the harness supports per-task --claude-tools, so a blanket --no-tools would change the grading contract. A per-run '--no-tools' harness flag forwarded to pi lanes (race lanes are self-contained by design) is the cheapest real step; sized at one flag + one doc paragraph + one dry-run regression, out of scope here per the plumbing-only bar.
